rationale: `named_funcs` is 321 of 328 (0.979), and the seven-definition gap is a decision rather than a miss. ATL-107 declines an entity for every `method`/`singleton_method` that sits under a block, because a block names nothing and so no scope path reaches the `def` (ADR-0032). Six of the seven are `method` under a `do_block`, one is under a `block`. Both shapes are real: `superclass.class_eval do def call ... end` (base.rb:267) attaches the method to the receiver rather than to the lexical class, and shared_examples.rb holds three sibling `def call`s that all claimed one uid. This reverses part of ATL-096, which started emitting these deliberately because they were invisible -- right about the invisibility, wrong about the remedy. Emitting nothing is the lesser failure: a missing entity is silence, a merged one is a confident wrong answer. A `def` under a *named* class inside a block is still an entity, because Ruby resolves that class's constant against the lexical nesting and a block is transparent to it; only `class << self` inside a block stays declined, since its `self` is the block's receiver. `calls` does not move, and that is the load-bearing check on the paragraph above: declining an entity relocates a call to the enclosing scope, and it must not lose it. 1,580 of 1,609 reach the graph before and after, and the check was stronger than the ratio -- across the full sinatra checkout the multiset of (file, callee, receiver) over all 14,345 CALLS edges is byte-identical across the change, with 686 edges changing only their `from` uid. duplicate_uids is 0, down from 8. Five were singleton-vs-instance: `def self.settings` and `def settings` in one class shared a qualified name, in both spellings (`def self.x`, and `def x` inside `class << self`). The singleton now takes a `self` segment -- `Sinatra.Base.self.settings` -- which mirrors the source, cannot collide with a real scope because `self` is a Ruby keyword, and changes the rarer of the two so the churn is bounded: over the full checkout 147 uids moved, every one of them a static_method, while all 629 instance methods and 23 constructors kept theirs. The other three were definitions inside an anonymous block, resolved by declining them. On the full checkout the same change takes 32 collisions to 0 and declines 93 definitions. The files were picked for the shapes that used to break the walker, not for the score -- `class << self` (base.rb), a class nested in a module (cookies.rb), `def` inside a `do_block` (delegator_test.rb, shared_examples.rb), `def self.` inside a `do_block` (json_csrf_spec.rb), `def` inside an `if` branch and behind an `if` modifier (cookies.rb, indifferent_hash.rb), and DSL block bodies throughout. The local-variable worry that motivates a lower `calls` floor in other languages does not apply here and was measured rather than assumed: across the whole sinatra checkout only 375 of 14,274 `call` nodes carry no receiver, no arguments and no block, and every one of them ends in `?` or `!` -- a form Ruby's lexer cannot confuse with a local read -- so the local-variable share of `call` nodes is 0%. Local variables show up only among bare `identifier` statements, where a binding set collected per `def`/`class`/`module` scope suppresses 20 of 32 candidates here (49 of 120 across the full checkout). The anonymous forms -- 178 `do_block`/`block`/`lambda` nodes with no entity -- are excluded from `named_funcs` by ADR-0031 and their calls attribute to the enclosing method or module, which is what carries `calls` this high in a codebase whose real work lives inside `get '/' do ... end`. METRIC CORRECTED 2026-08-06: `calls` read 1.005 on sinatra, above 1.0, because the denominator counted only `call` nodes while the walker also emits an edge for a bare identifier standing alone as a statement -- Ruby's implicit `self` call (`content_type`, `pass`, `not_found`). Those 146 nodes were in the numerator and not the denominator. `identifier` now counts as a call in statement position only, since the same node type spells every parameter and variable read. sinatra reads 0.995 against a denominator of 14,420, which is the honest number. METRIC CORRECTED 2026-08-06 (ATL-107): named_funcs briefly read 0.979 here and 0.896 on sinatra because the 7 (respectively 93) definitions ADR-0032 declines -- a `def` inside an anonymous block, which no qualified name can identify -- stayed in the denominator. Asserting their capture measured the opposite of the decision, the same defect TypeScript's `method_definition` had. `named_blocked_by_scope` now excludes them, resolved against `named_scope_anchors` so a named class or module inside a block re-anchors the chain and its methods stay asserted. The denominator is now the 321 definitions that must be entities, all 321 are captured, and the floor is exact 1.0 -- tighter than the 0.978 it replaces, not looser.
